findings.description: Port 22 (SSH) is open to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing any host on the internet to attempt administrative access to the instance. SSH should be restricted to known management CIDR ranges or accessed via a bastion/VPN.

The user_data script embeds a live-looking AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext. This data is stored in the instance metadata/user-data (retrievable via the EC2 API and IMDS) and in Terraform state, creating a durable credential leak.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (or a kms_key_id), so data at rest on this volume is unencrypted, violating encryption-at-rest requirements for sensitive workloads.

The snapshot is taken from the unencrypted portal_server_disk volume and has no encryption settings of its own, so the backup data is also stored unencrypted and could be shared/copied without protection.

The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration) and no public access block, leaving log data unencrypted and potentially exposed if bucket policy/ACLs are later loosened.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet, especially combined with the portal_server instance and permissive security group placed in this subnet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes any instance placed in this subnet to receive a public IP by default, expanding the network attack surface without explicit per-instance opt-in.
